Mahean
Magamemnon

Hi, I’m Mahean. I recently founded Foresight Machines.

I study computational sciences at Minerva University, a new kind of university backed by Benchmark, and spend each semester living in a different country. When I’m not abroad, I live in the great city of San Francisco, California.

Before that, I spent a year on the core investment team at M13, focused on AI and energy startups and building software for automation.

EmailX / maheanmm

Interests

  • 01Simulation→

    Most decisions are made once, with no rehearsal. A good model changes that: you can run the same choice thousands of times, vary the assumptions, and see where it breaks before anything real is at stake.

    I’m interested in how far that idea can be pushed, from a single company to a city to a whole economy.

  • 02Superforecasting→

    Some people are measurably better at predicting world events than the experts, and the reasons are learnable: thinking in probabilities, updating often, and keeping score.

    I like it because it turns judgment into something you can check. It is also the input every simulation needs: a model is only as good as the forecasts you feed it.

  • 03Augmented reality→

    Computing that lives in the world around us instead of behind a screen. The hardest part is the optics: getting a bright, wide image into something the size of ordinary glasses.

    That is where metamaterials come in. They are structures engineered at a scale smaller than the wavelength of light, and they can bend it in ways no ordinary lens can. They may be what finally makes the hardware disappear.

  • 04Capital→

    Ambitious ideas usually need money long before they can show results, and most funding is built for shorter horizons than they require.

    I spent a year on the investing side at M13, and I still think about how to fund things that take a decade to prove out.

  • 05Bioluminescence→

    Some living things make their own light. Researchers have now engineered plants that glow, and the obvious next question is how far that goes: light that grows instead of being wired, and organisms that report on their own health by changing colour.

    It is also simply one of the most beautiful things in nature.

  • 06Space economy→

    The cost of reaching orbit has fallen by more than ten times, and the number of satellites up there is growing faster than ever. A real economy is forming above us.

    It comes with a problem: debris. A single collision can create thousands of fragments, and enough of them could make the most useful orbits unusable. Keeping orbit clean is a precondition for everything else we want to do there.

  • 07Strategy games→

    Chess, Go and StarCraft are small worlds where you plan under uncertainty, against another mind, and find out quickly when you are wrong.

    They are also where much of modern AI first learned to plan. I play them for the same reason I like forecasting: the feedback is honest.

  • 08Climate & environment→

    Energy that is abundant, cheap and clean at the same time. I’m most interested in the parts that decide whether it actually happens: generation, storage, the grid, and the capital and policy that set how fast it gets built.

  • 09Aesthetics→

    Buildings, objects and interfaces that are a pleasure to be around. Beauty is usually treated as a luxury. I think it is closer to a requirement, because people look after the things they find beautiful.
